questions.description: e.g., downtown, suburban, rural.

questions.title: How much of a role do you want the name to play in branding?
questions.description: e.g., very important, moderately important, not at all.

questions.title: What words or phrases do you love or dislike?

questions.title: Do you have any specific words or phrases that you would like to avoid?
questions.description: e.g., bakery, sweet, delicious, bakery.

input: Brainstorm a name for my new bakery

verdict.notes: Set B has notable redundancy — Q6 asks about words/phrases you "love or dislike" and Q7 immediately asks about words/phrases to "avoid," making them largely overlapping. It also misses a key creative angle that Set A captures: whether the owner wants their personal name or story woven into the name, which is a highly relevant and actionable distinction for bakery naming. Q5 about how much the name should "play in branding" is vague and generic rather than concrete to naming brainstorming.

questions.title: What are my key achievements and accomplishments in previous roles?
questions.description: Please share specific examples of your successes that demonstrate your product management abilities.

questions.title: What is my current salary and compensation expectations for a product manager role?
questions.description: Please provide an estimate of your current salary and how you would like to position yourself in this role.

questions.title: Do you have any specific industries or sectors you are targeting for this role?
questions.description: Are there any particular industries or companies you are interested in working with?

input: Update my resume for a product manager role

verdict.notes: Set B has several critical flaws: questions are phrased in first person ("I am applying for," "my current salary") which is robotic and confusing for a coach-to-user interaction; Q6 asks about salary/compensation which is irrelevant to updating a resume; Q1 and Q2 are partially redundant (role + responsibilities overlap with a job posting question); and it never asks whether the user has an existing resume — the most fundamental unknown for this task. Set A is more focused, natural, and covers the essentials more cleanly.
